gaps.sentence: The training course will ___ you to work abroad (QUALIFY).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: qualify. A base verb follows 'will'.

gaps.sentence: I'm afraid your passport is ___ — it expired last month (VALID).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: it has expired
gaps.explanation: An expired document is invalid (in- + valid); an adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (POPULAR) of the band grew after the film.
This grant will ___ her to study abroad (ABLE).
gaps.hint: positive verb needed: make it possible (en-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix en- forms the verb: enable means to make able. 'Disable' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: The two countries signed a peace ___ (TREAT).
gaps.explanation: A peace treaty is a formal agreement; 'treatment' means medical care or the way you behave towards someone.

gaps.sentence: The train arrived ___ , despite the snow (PUNCTUAL).
gaps.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'arrived': punctually (-ly). 'Punctuality' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: She speaks English ___ for a beginner (REMARKABLE).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'speaks': remarkably (-ly).

gaps.sentence: He is very ___ about local history (KNOW).
gaps.explanation: 'Knowledgeable about something' means knowing a lot about it; it is the adjective form of 'knowledge'.
